In the first hours, the dark would feel like any other night.
Picture a small village high in the mountains.
The ground, the walls and the lake still hold the warmth of yesterday.
On a normal night, that warmth would carry the village through until sunrise.
But that heat would slowly leak away into space, and nothing would come to replace it.
Every plant on Earth would stop making food the moment the light was gone.
The grass, the crops, the trees on these slopes.
No harvest would ever ripen again.
For now, they would wait, living on what they had stored.
Solar panels on the roofs would produce nothing at all.
The temperature would keep falling, hour after hour.
Ten degrees.
Five.
The lake would steam in the freezing air, giving up its heat.
People would light fires and turn up the heating.
Shops would sell out of candles, blankets and firewood.
The square would empty as everyone went indoors.
Power stations would burn through fuel faster than ever, as the whole world tried to keep warm.
By the end of the first day, frost would creep over the rooftops.
Moisture in the air would start to fall as snow.
And there would be no morning.
The clocks would say it is day.
The sky would say it is night.
Birds would stay in their nests, waiting for a dawn that never comes.
And it would stay night.
